As of 2019 local discrimination coverage existed only in the city of Buenos Aires and in Rosario, with no national statute; earlier civil-union schemes were endorsed in the city of Buenos Aires and one province in 2002–2003 and in two inland cities in 2007 and 2009, all without adoption, before a nationwide scheme took effect in 2015. Documented trans community infrastructure is capital-based: a publicly funded Casa Trans and the Mocha Celis school, both in Buenos Aires.

AUS.diversity: The record documents a jurisdiction-by-jurisdiction patchwork, not a single national picture. Gender-identity discrimination coverage is uneven: protected federally since 2013, but among the states and territories three reach sexual orientation only, three add gender identity, and two cover neither. Custody-placement standards are documented for Queensland alone.
